title: The birth of rock'n'roll
subject: art
description: In the mid-1950s, black blues and white country merged: Elvis, Chuck Berry and Little Richard invented rock'n'roll.

hero.hook: A scream, an electric guitar, and teenage America has its music.

blocks.text: Rock'n'roll did not emerge out of nowhere in the middle of the **1950** years. In the United States, he merged music long separated by racial barriers: blues, country and . [[Gospel]]
Three figures carry the break: **Elvis Presley**, **Chuck Berry** and **Little Richard**. More than a style, it is a youth culture, and a mirror of the tensions of the . [[Segregation]]

sections.title: Blues, country and rhythm and blues

blocks.text: Until then, two worlds coexisted in the South: black culture (electric blues, gospel) and white culture (country). The bridge is called : an urban and electrified version of the blues which attracted, from the end of the 1940s, white youth in search of rhythm. [[Rhythm and blues (R&B)]]

**rockabilly** is born, a country and blues hybrid. **Elvis Presley**, from Tupelo, grew up between Pentecostal churches and Beale Street blues. In **1954**, at the producer  in Memphis, he recorded *That's All Right*. But  remains the rule: black artists often remain confined to marginal circuits, while a white performer can cross the national market. [[Sam Phillips]] [[Segregation in the American music industry]]
The term "rock'n'roll" first referred to the pitching of a ship, then, in the blues of the 1920s, to the sexual act, before being popularized by DJ . [[Alan Freed]]
At , Elvis becomes the icon. His moving body shocked puritanical America and sealed the alliance between rock and adolescence. [[Sun Records]]

blocks.caption: Elvis at Sun Records: rock finds its face.

blocks.text: **Chuck Berry** provides the structure: the guitar **riff**, a repeated motif which becomes the backbone of the piece. He sings about cars, high school, freedom. **Little Richard** screams and hits the piano standing up: raw energy inherited from gospel fervor.

blocks.caption: Chuck Berry: the guitar riff as the grammar of rock.
Little Richard: the cry and the piano as an explosion.

blocks.text: In 1956, on *The Ed Sullivan Show*, the cameras only filmed Elvis above the waist: his hip movements were considered too scandalous.

For the first time, black and white teenagers share the same idols, despite the . But integration remains asymmetrical. The industry is multiplying s: watered-down white versions of black hits, better promoted on the radio. Pat Boone's *Tutti Frutti* outsold Little Richard's original for a long time. [[Jim Crow laws]] [[Covers]]
Despite these spoliations, rock nourishes the spirit of . By breaking parental codes, the youth of the 1950s began a moral and racial questioning of America. [[Civil Rights Movement]]
Chuck Berry didn't take his band on tour: he hired local musicians in each city, to save money and avoid racial tensions at the hotel.

sections.title: From the British Invasion to Legacy

blocks.text: Around **1960**, the first wind runs out of steam (Elvis to the army, Little Richard to religion). But the genre has already conquered the United Kingdom. The **Beatles** and the **Rolling Stones** reinterpret American standards: the “British Invasion” transforms rock into album art and protest. Without the breach of **1954**, the countercultures of the 1960s would not have had the same sonic engine.

blocks.text: Born in 1954 from the fusion between rhythm and blues and country, the rock'n'roll of Elvis, Berry and Little Richard gave young people a first common language against segregation.
